title: Pip and the Tin
checkpoint: Reception Autumn 1, week 3 — after s, a, t, p, i, n, m, d (Learning — Phase 2)
note_for_grown_ups: Every word here can be sounded out with the sounds taught so far, including Pip's name (p-i-p). 'is' is a tricky word: the s says /z/.

pages.illustration: An old dented biscuit tin lying on its side in the grass with Pip sitting neatly inside it, only his head and tuft showing over the rim. Cosy and comic.
Same tin from a low angle so it looms — Pip's surprised face peering over the edge, feet braced. The tin should read as an adventure, not a trap.

pages.text: Tap, tap, tap — Pip taps a tin.
pages.illustration: Pip standing on the upturned tin drumming it with both feet. Show the noise as the tin visibly wobbling and a startled ladybird taking off, not as symbols.
Pip curled up asleep inside the tin with his head tucked under one wing, evening light slanting in through the open end. Very still and warm.

pages.text: Pip sat. Pip sat. Pip naps.
pages.illustration: Pull right back: the tin small in a big grassy garden at dusk, a contented sparrow-shaped bump inside it, first star showing above the shed.
